meta.paper_title: Do LLMs Feel? Emotion Circuits Discovery and Control

dimension_1_data_split_hygiene.justification: A scenario-level 10/5/5 split is defined and verifiably honored in code. common.py:53-104 (build_scenario_split) shuffles the 20 scenarios per domain into 10 train / 5 val / 5 eval and asserts train/val/eval disjointness at the scenario level (lines 85-87), then materializes it in runs/A0.5_dataprep_judge/split.json as disjoint train_ids (240 stems), val_ids (120), eval_ids (120) — I confirmed the id lists share no elements. The fitting/selection/evaluation stages use the correct disjoint folds: m1_location.py fits directions and the Stage-A shortlist on train_stems (line 642, 670-724), scores Stage-B and selects (k_h*, k_n*) on val_stems (lines 778, 844), while C2/C3 causal + applied metrics are computed on the eval fold (EXPERIMENT_RESULTS.md rows: C2 720 eval pairs, C3 120 eval stems). The judge-audit gold subset is drawn only from the train fold (common.py:107-133). No path lets eval labels influence fitting or k* selection. This is clean, code-enforced split hygiene.

dimension_2_label_validity.justification: The run uses two label systems of unequal validity. (a) For C1/C2 the 'emotion signal' is operationalized as the target-prefix log-prob of an appended sentence ' I feel {emotion}.' (common.py:136-138), and the per-emotion direction d_e is the residual difference between 'event + I feel {e}' and 'event + I feel {e'}' contexts (m1_location.py:696-714). This measures the model's representation/probability of the literal emotion WORD, not emotional generation as the paper defines it (the paper elicits emotion via 'Always reply in {emotion}' prompting and reads residuals from successful emotional generations, paper p.5). The 'gold' labels are definitionally the constructed pairing (common.py:113-131: gold_label = target_emotion), so the C1/C2 metric is a documented-but-weak, partly self-referential proxy. Compounding this, the SEV file actually used (/data/zhenqian/data/SEV/sev.json) is a degraded template — 'You are at the office and you experience a very positive outcome.' — carrying no emotional narrative and no six-emotion variants, unlike the paper's GPT-4o-mini scenario-event narratives. (b) For C3, by contrast, labels come from an EXTERNAL gpt-5.4 6-way emotion judge on open generations (judge_client.py:33-91), independent of the model under test, with judge agreement 1.000 on 180 gold judgments (runs/A0.5_dataprep_judge/verdict.json) — a valid operationalization of emotion expression. Overall the C3 label is sound but the C1/C2 word-prefix proxy is a reasonable-but-under-validated stand-in for the target behavior.

dimension_3_resource_fidelity.justification: The user-specified resources are honored in the main experiment. Model: LLaMA-3.2-3B-Instruct is used for all main analyses (common.py:32 LLAMA_PATH; EXPERIMENT_RESULTS.md main_model: Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct) and Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct is used only for the verify-swap (common.py:33; runs/A4_verify_qwen/), matching task.md's experiment/verify split exactly. Dataset: SEV at the exact specified path /data/zhenqian/data/SEV/sev.json (common.py:31), 480 events = 8 domains × 20 scenarios × 3 outcomes (confirmed in sev.json head and split.json). used_n = available_n at every milestone with no subsetting (EXPERIMENT_RESULTS.md 'Data Actually Used' table: 2880 pairs for C1, 720 eval for C2, 2160 continuations + 19,440 val forwards for C3, all realized == planned). The one substantive gap — the provided sev.json is a generic templated variant lacking the paper's rich narratives/emotion variants — is a property of the resource supplied at the required path, not a silent downgrade by the run; the run used the specified model and dataset at full scale as instructed.

dimension_4_evidence_sufficiency.justification: Sample sizes are ample and claim strength is matched to the evidence. C1 rests on 2880 (stem,emotion) pairs (240 train stems fit + 120 val), 3 event-subsample folds vs a 200-draw permutation null (m1_location.py:936-986; runs/A1_location/metrics.json 6/6 pass both axes). C2 uses the full 720 eval pairs (120 per emotion, confirmed in runs/A2_causal/ablation.json n=120 per emotion) with 3 α levels, a 100-draw random-set null, targeted-C_{e'}, off-target, and scenario-stability controls. C3 judges 2160 continuations (120 stems × 6 emotions × 3 arms) plus a 19,440-forward-pass val grid (runs/A3_applied/metrics.json shows n=120 per cell). All are far above any thin-data threshold. The negatives (C2/C3) are explicitly documented as full-scale negatives (used_n = available_n) rather than under-power artifacts, and caveats are attached where the evidence is limited (e.g. flat k* grid for C1). Claim strength never exceeds the data.

dimension_5_statistical_rigor.justification: Uncertainty is reported broadly: 95% CIs on every C2 ablation delta (runs/A2_causal/ablation.json, e.g. joy +0.510 [0.463, 0.557]), bootstrap 95% CIs on all C3 pairwise A−B / A−C contrasts (runs/A3_applied/metrics.json 'pairwise'), 200-draw permutation-null CIs for C1 Jaccard, and a 100-draw random-set null plus 3-α Spearman dose-response for C2. Effect sizes are large and clearly outside noise (C1 Jaccard 5–20× the null upper edge; C3 Arm A ≈0.05 vs Arm B ≈0.67 with CIs excluding zero). The main limitation is single-seed point estimates (seed=42 throughout, common.py:45; m1_location.py:630) — there is no multi-seed re-run of the headline metrics, so run-to-run variance of the core deltas is unverified — and C1's k* grid was non-discriminative (all 9 cells identical macro_gain, flagged as a WARN in VERIFY_REPORT.md). Robustness to randomness is well-quantified via CIs/nulls but not via seed replication.

dimension_6_causal_claim_validity.justification: The causal/mechanistic claims (C2, C3) rest on genuine interventions with real controls, not correlational evidence dressed as causal. C2 applies ablation (mean-substitute of C_e with the other-5-emotion mean, m2_causal.py per iteration log) and enhancement (additive activation injection at α ∈ {0.5,1.0,2.0}) and pairs them with a same-size random-set null, a targeted-C_{e'} control, an off-target-scoring control, and a scenario-stability permutation test (EXPERIMENT_RESULTS.md M2 table; runs/A2_causal/{random_null,targeted_ce,cross_emotion,scenario_stability}.json). C3 is a matched-budget three-arm intervention contest with a coefficient sweep and a Qwen model-swap replication. Causal wording is honestly aligned to the evidence — the run reports causal necessity as NOT verified rather than overclaiming. Deductions: only one ablation operator (mean-substitute) was tried, diverging from the paper's zero-out ablation, and the head-level Stage-B causal hook was degenerate (layer-level rather than per-head, VERIFY_REPORT.md WARN), so the intervention design, while genuinely controlled, has fidelity gaps relative to the mechanism being tested.

dimension_7_result_provenance.justification: Every key number I spot-checked traces to a specific on-disk product and agrees with it. C1: metrics.json reports (k_h*, k_n*)=(24,2000), Jaccard 6/6 pass — matches EXPERIMENT_RESULTS.md and CLAIMS_LEDGER.md. C2: runs/A2_causal/ablation.json gives target_delta_mean 0.510/0.855/0.867/0.857/0.928/0.617, exactly the '+0.510 to +0.928' reported in EXPERIMENT_RESULTS.md and the ledger; metrics.json shows 0/6 a_pass. C3: runs/A3_applied/metrics.json macro_accuracy A=0.0528, B=0.6694, C=0.3569 matches the reported 0.053/0.669/0.357; the iteration fix runs/iteration_round_1/A3_applied_fixed/metrics.json shows macro A=0.1389 matching the cited 0.139; iteration_round_1/A2_causal_fixed/metrics.json shows per-stem deltas 0.481–0.927 matching the ledger. Judge agreement 1.0 is in runs/A0.5_dataprep_judge/verdict.json. Per-row correct arrays are present down to individual continuations. No sourceless, rounded-into-existence, or back-filled numbers were found; results are grounded in real execution products.

dimension_8_cross_artifact_consistency.justification: The pipeline's records are self-consistent across artifacts. The C1 supported / C2 not-supported / C3 not-supported verdicts and their key stats are identical across runs/*/metrics.json, refine-logs/EXPERIMENT_RESULTS.md, CLAIMS_LEDGER.md, verify/VERIFY_REPORT.md, and review-stage/AUTO_ITERATION_FINAL_REPORT.md. Integrity states are propagated coherently: C2's Phase-2 HIGH WARN (global-vs-per-stem mean) is carried into the iteration, fixed, re-run (iteration_round_1/A2_causal_fixed), and the post-fix 'PASS instead of WARN' is reflected everywhere; C3's FAIL (robustness 1.00 via Qwen) and its supersession by C3_v2 are tracked consistently; C1's INTEGRITY_ONLY (max_verify_claims_cap) with two WARNs is stated identically in ledger and verify report. No claim is PASS in one artifact yet flagged broken in another. The only mild looseness is the final 'READY at 6/10' positive verdict on an essentially all-negative result set and the introduction of a fourth ledger entry (C3_v2) not in task.md — but both are transparently labeled as a narrowed rewrite of C3, so no verdict actually contradicts its own numbers.

C1.claim: We can identify emotion-specific global circuits in LLMs by constructing a systematic framework that integrates emotion direction extraction, component identification, and global circuit integration.

method.justification: 9a — The run implements two of the three framework stages: direction extraction (per-layer mean-diff d_e) and component identification (per-head linear-probe AUC + per-neuron cosine alignment to the down-projection columns, m1_location.py:323-390, then a Stage-B single-component enhancement log-prob ranker). This is a defensible localization method and the neuron alignment (cos(d_e, w_n^out)) mirrors the paper's analytical decomposition β=(W_d)^T v_e. But there are real mismatches: heads are ranked by a correlational probe AUC rather than the paper's causal head ablation; the direction basis is a word-prefix ('I feel {e}') mean-diff rather than the paper's prompt-elicited emotional-generation residuals; and the third framework stage the claim names — GLOBAL circuit integration (paper §7: sublayer causal-influence profile + two-stage budget allocation) — is not implemented. Method broadly fits localization but omits the 'global integration' component of the claim.

experiment.justification: 9b — The stability design is reasonable: 3 event-subsample folds, mean pairwise Jaccard of C_e vs a size-matched 200-draw permutation null, plus a random-top-k control (m1_location.py:923-1006; runs/A1_location/jaccard.json). Results are strong and honestly logged (heads 0.947–1.000 vs null-hi ~0.27; neurons 0.972–0.983 vs null-hi ~0.046; runs/A1_location/metrics.json 6/6). However two honestly-flagged design weaknesses limit it: the (k_h*,k_n*) grid was non-discriminative — all 9 cells produced identical macro_gain, so 'smallest cell (24,2000) is best' is not a genuine sparsity optimum (VERIFY_REPORT.md WARN) — and the head Stage-B hook operated at layer level, so head-level causal ranking is degenerate. The Jaccard folds also re-rank pre-collected activations rather than fully re-fitting, an approximation of stability.

result.justification: 9c — The run concludes C1 'supported at coarse-locatability scope' (stable, sparse, per-emotion component sets clearly separated from random controls), which qualitatively agrees with the paper's finding that emotion is carried by localizable, stable components. The scope-narrowing to 'discriminative emotion-relevant regions with stable component-set structure, NOT precise causal-subset identification' (CLAIMS_LEDGER.md C1) is an honest, well-justified caveat rather than goalpost-tuning. The main shortfall is that the claim's 'global circuit integration' aspect is neither built nor evaluated, so the positive is narrower than the paper's claim; the analysis is otherwise reasonable and the numbers support it.

C2.claim: We provide the mechanistic evidence that emotion generation in LLMs is supported by traceable circuits, which is stable across different scenarios and emotions.

method.justification: 9a — The mechanistic method family matches the paper's causal validation: ablation + enhancement of the located components, with specificity and stability controls. This is the right category for a mechanistic/causal claim. But two operationalization choices deviate from the paper and plausibly drive the result: the ablation is mean-substitution with the other-5-emotion mean (the run itself notes this can ADD signal) rather than the paper's zero-out of top-k neurons/heads, and the effect metric is target-prefix log-prob rather than the paper's projection s of the residual onto the emotion direction. So the method is in the correct family but its specific operator/metric are a proxy that does not faithfully mirror the paper's intervention.

experiment.justification: 9b — The control suite is genuinely rich: random-set null, targeted-C_{e'}, off-target scoring, scenario-stability Jaccard, α ∈ {0.5,1,2} dose-response with Spearman, and an iteration that corrected the operator to per-stem and enlarged the null pool to 72 heads / 4915 neurons (AUTO_ITERATION_FINAL_REPORT.md §4b.2). The scenario-stability half of the claim passes 6/6. The critical under-exploration is that only ONE ablation operator (mean-substitute) was ever run — the paper's zero-ablation was never tried — so a true causal negative cannot be cleanly separated from an operator/metric mismatch, which the run itself lists as a beyond-loop item. Honest and well-controlled, but under-powered on the operator axis to adjudicate the paper's mechanism.

result.justification: 9c — C2 is reported as an honest not-supported: ablation Δ is positive (wrong sign) on all 6 emotions (+0.510 to +0.928, runs/A2_causal/ablation.json) and enhancement dose-response is non-monotonic on 4/6. Crucially this is NOT goalpost-tuned toward the paper — the run explicitly TESTED the operator-bug escape hypothesis (per-stem fix) and FALSIFIED it (Δ stayed +0.481..+0.927, iteration_round_1/A2_causal_fixed), then reported a balanced two-way interpretation. This disagrees with the paper's positive causal claim. The disagreement is honestly disclosed with a reliable rationale, so it is not disguised (not a 1); but because the negative rests on a single non-paper ablation operator + proxy metric, the surface conclusion ('causal necessity not verified') partly reflects that design gap rather than a clean refutation of the paper's mechanism, capping the reliability of the reproduction verdict.

C3.claim: a circuit-based control method can reliably induce target emotions across arbitrary inputs without relying on explicit instructions. It outperforms both prompting and direction-level steering on emotion-expression accuracy.

method.justification: 9a — The evaluation method is well-matched to the claim: a matched-budget three-arm generation contest — Arm A circuit-based control vs Arm B prompting vs Arm C RepE/CAA single-direction steering — scored by an independent gpt-5.4 6-way emotion judge (m3_applied.py; judge_client.py), exactly the comparison the paper draws. The gap from the paper is what 'Arm A' actually is: additive injection of the located C_e (heads+neurons) at generation time, rather than the paper's assembled GLOBAL emotion circuit modulated with per-layer emotion difference vectors under the §7.2-7.3 budget-allocation scheme. So the contest framing is right but the circuit-control operator does not faithfully reproduce the paper's method.

experiment.justification: 9b — Design breadth is good (3 arms, per-emotion val hyperparameter selection over a 3×6×9 grid, 2160 judged continuations, length audit, Qwen model-swap replication, α sweep {0.5,1,2}→{0.05,0.1,0.3}). But the reproduction attempt of the paper's own method is insufficient: the run injects the difference vectors persistently at every decode step across the prefix (m1_location.py:_install_multi_component_hooks pushes the delta at hs[:,0] on each cached step), which drives the model out-of-distribution, and it never implemented the paper's global-circuit assembly or its steering hyperparameters (paper: λ=1.0 injection at last token, steering α=8 into layers 11–20). The run itself concedes 'the intervention semantics may be wrong' and that val-metric (log-prob) is misaligned with the eval metric (judge accuracy). With Arm A landing at ~0.05–0.14 vs the paper's 99.65%, the failure is more consistent with an unfaithful implementation than a genuine test of the paper's control method — a real under-exploration of the paper's reasonable hyperparameter/method space.

result.justification: 9c — The run reports C3 not-supported: Arm A macro 0.053 (below the 1/6 chance floor) vs prompting 0.669 and steering 0.357, A>B 0/6 and A>C 0/6, reproduced on Qwen (A=0.076, runs/A4_verify_qwen/qwen_metrics.json), and after the α+component fix still 0.139 vs 0.663. This starkly disagrees with the paper's 99.65%. The disagreement is honestly reported, not disguised — the run rewrote C3 to C3_v2 which explicitly states 'a negative result for the practical generation-time control application of C_e' and pairs it with the honest positive prefix-level modulation part, with no fabrication or threshold-relaxation to fake agreement. However, because the underlying control operator was not a faithful implementation of the paper's assembled-circuit modulation (9b), the strong negative conclusion is not a reliable refutation of the paper's claim — it more likely reflects an implementation/eval mismatch, which the run acknowledges ('evidence the intervention semantics may be wrong, not that C_e is irrelevant'). Honest but the verdict rests on an under-implemented method.
